title: TickTockStack: In-Datapath Current Imbalance Elimination Using Clocked Differential Logic in a Voltage Stacked Vector Processor
problem: Voltage stacking mitigates PDN loss but suffers from voltage ripple and power delivery loss due to current imbalance of stacked circuits. CMOS logic activity variations create data-dependent imbalance.
motivation: Reduce power delivery loss in high-power-density chips while maintaining frequency and reliability.
method: Voltage-stacked vector processor with architecture-circuit co-optimization: datapath implemented using clocked dual-rail domino logic with constant activity factor and differential structure; register file as fully differential latch-based structure with symmetrical multiplexers; single-ended CMOS control logic. Synchronized execution across vector lanes minimizes control-driven variation.
key_novelty: In-datapath current imbalance elimination via clocked differential logic with constant activity factor.
contributions: Clocked dual-rail domino datapath design with constant activity factor
Fully differential register file with symmetrical architecture

metrics.other: 6.2x reduction in stack voltage ripple; 33.5% lower PDN power loss; no frequency limitations vs subthreshold methods

limitations: Technique specific to vector processors; generalization to scalar or other architectures unclear.
primary_theme: differential logic for voltage-stacked vector processor
